GLIMT

180minutes
48solder joints
difficulty

A 32 x 8 pixel clock for your smart home

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

30GLIMT-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    5VGND3V3GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    5VDC jack 5V · 1000uF + · Panel 5V · ESP32 VIN
    GNDDC jack GND · 1000uF - · Panel GND · ESP32 GND · Btn R 2 · Btn sel 2 · Btn L 2
    MATRIXESP32 D32 · 470R 1
    rdata_2470R 2 · Panel DIN
    3V3ESP32 3V3 · BME280 VCC · LDR 1
    GNDESP32 GND.2 · BME280 GND · 10k 2 · Piezo -
    I2C_SDAESP32 D21 · BME280 SDA
    I2C_SCLESP32 D22 · BME280 SCL
    LDRLDR 2 · 10k 1 · ESP32 D35
    BUZZERESP32 D15 · Piezo +
    BTN_LEFTESP32 D26 · Btn L 1
    BTN_SELECTESP32 D27 · Btn sel 1
    BTN_RIGHTESP32 D14 · Btn R 1
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
31GLIMT-WIRE-1

Glimt is built

Glimt is a self-built AWTRIX pixel clock: a 32 x 8 RGB LED matrix behind a diffuser, driven by a classic ESP32 wired exactly like the Ulanzi TC001, so AWTRIX 3 or AWTRIX NG run on it on their default pin map. It shows the time, weather, now-playing and Home Assistant notifications pushed over MQTT or HTTP, with three buttons, a light sensor for auto-brightness, a room sensor and a beeper.
